title: Slice thermal-aware microkernel placement and proactive prefill windowing
creator: Ava R. Chen
description:
Problem:  We observe tail-latency and throughput degradation on multi-tenant H100/L40S clusters under sustained load when MIG slices share thermal/power budgets with variable A100-class neighbors. Current kernel-selection is agnostic to per-slice thermal headroom and global clock-steering decisions, which leads to reactive throttling and expensive prefill stalls during bursty traffic.

Goal: Implement a per-MIG-slice, thermal-aware microkernel placement strategy plus a proactive prefill windowing mechanism that: 1) maps microkernels to slices honoring thermal headroom and NVLink locality, 2) staggers/advances prefill windows to avoid simultaneous KV-cache spikes, and 3) integrates with clock governor feedback to minimize thermal-induced clock drops while keeping 99th percentile latency below SLO.

Scope: H100 and L40S primary; A10 considered for mixed-fleet experiments. Work includes telemetry additions, microkernel ranking heuristic, prefill window scheduler, and an emergent fallback policy for emergency clock-steer events.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 99th percentile token latency for 2k-context chat workload improves by >=15% under contended MIG packing compared to baseline (runtime-1.24) in internal testbed
2) Throughput under synthetic bursty arrival (Poisson with peak factor 8) shows <10% degradation vs ideal when thermal headroom is at 60%
3) No increase in error rate or OOMs in production canary across three customer tenants over 48 hours
4) Telemetry exposed: per-slice thermal headroom, microkernel-placement decisions, prefill-window start/end, and clock-steer events (dashboard and traces)
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Spike completed comparing static vs dynamic microkernel ranking — dynamic ranking reduced median latency but increased scheduler jitter; decided to prototype hybrid approach
2026-03-05: Chose thermal headroom metric = (T_junction_limit - T_current)/T_junction_limit as primary signal for slice ranking to avoid vendor clock-throttle counters reliance
2026-03-07: Opted to implement prefill windowing as adjustable soft-quota (ms) per slice instead of hard token limits to preserve tail latency for low-volume clients
2026-03-10: Rollout plan approved by SRE and PM; emergency fallback will default to single-slice conservative kernel and disable staggering during critical clocks-off events
architecture_notes: Microkernel placement lives in the runtime's scheduler component. New table: SliceState (flat telemetry exported) used by kernel-ranker. Prefill windowing hooks added to request ingress path and KV-cache admission. Interaction with clock governor via pub/sub topic: clock-governor.events. Keep fast path lock-free by caching last placement per-model for 200ms.
tradeoffs:
- Aggressive ranking reduces thermal risk but can force less-optimal kernels for some sequence lengths (possible small QoE regression).
- Prefill windowing reduces simultaneous KV spikes but adds scheduling complexity and potential for added latency to individual prefill ops.
- Using thermal headroom instead of vendor counters trades absolute accuracy for faster, vendor-agnostic response and reduced dependency on privileged telemetry.
test_plan: Unit tests for kernel-ranker heuristics and prefill-window timers
Integration e2e tests on multi-MIG H100 lab with synthetic workloads (Chat-2k, Summarize-8k)
A/B canary: 10% fleet on runtime-1.26-canary, monitor latency, throughput, thermal alarms for 72h
Fault injection: force clock-steer event and verify fallback disables staggering and logs event
benchmark_results: Spike 2026-03-02: dynamic-hybrid prototype showed 12% median token latency reduction and 18% 99th under controlled MIG pressure. Baseline numbers and raw traces uploaded to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/3X-mig-thermal/placement-spikes
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Lab validation on H100/L40S mixed rack (3 nodes) — run 48h soak
Phase 1: Internal canary on non-customer dev cluster — 1d smoke then 7d soak
Phase 2: Customer canaries (3 tenants) with manual rollback triggers (SLO breach, OOM, thermal alarms) — 72h
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 50% fleet over 2 weeks with automated rollback on anomalies
Phase 4: Full rollout and merge runtime-1.26 into main
observability_tasks: Add metrics: slice_thermal_headroom, kernel_choice_id, prefill_window_us, prefill_pending_count; add trace spans for placement decision and prefill admission; create Grafana dashboard and alert if prefill_pending_count exceeds threshold for >30s
implementation_todos: Telemetry: expose per-slice temperature and estimated power headroom (ENG infra + hw-telemetry)
Kernel-ranker: implement hybrid scoring (thermal headroom * locality_score + seq_len_fit)
Prefill-scheduler: soft-window controller with jittered start offsets per-slice
Fallback: single-slice conservative kernel and disable windowing on clock-governor.emergency
Docs: Update runtime ops guide and release notes
